title: The Download: Claude's inner workings and OpenAI's "super app"

paragraphs.text: This is today's edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what's going on in the world of technology.
paragraphs.translation: 這是《The Download》的今日版本，這是我們的平日電子報，每天為你精選科技界的最新動態。

paragraphs.text: Anthropic found a hidden space where Claude puzzles over concepts
paragraphs.translation: Anthropic 發現了 Claude 用來思考概念的隱藏空間

paragraphs.text: The AI firm Anthropic has got the clearest glimpse yet at what’s really going on inside large language models as they answer questions or carry out tasks. What they found ranges from the mundane to the unnerving.
paragraphs.translation: AI 公司 Anthropic 目前已經對大型語言模型在回答問題或執行任務時，內部究竟發生了什麼事，獲得了迄今為止最清楚的一瞥。他們的發現從平凡無奇到令人不安都有。

paragraphs.text: Researchers at the company built a tool called the Jacobian lens (or J-lens) and used it to uncover a hidden area, which they named the J-space, inside its flagship LLM, Claude.
paragraphs.translation: 該公司的研究人員打造了一項名為「雅可比透鏡」（Jacobian lens，簡稱 J-lens）的工具，並用它在其旗艦大型語言模型 Claude 內部，發掘出一個他們命名為「J 空間」（J-space）的隱藏區域。

paragraphs.text: The J-space contains words related to the response a model is working on but may not ultimately produce. If Claude were a person (which it is not), you might say these hidden words reveal what’s on its mind before it actually speaks.
paragraphs.translation: J 空間中包含了與模型正在構思的回應相關、但最終未必會產出的字詞。如果 Claude 是一個人（當然它不是），你或許可以說，這些隱藏的字詞揭露了它「開口說話」之前腦中所想的事。

paragraphs.text: Read the full story on what they found.
paragraphs.translation: 閱讀完整報導，了解他們的發現。

paragraphs.text: The must-reads
paragraphs.translation: 必讀重點

paragraphs.text: I’ve combed the internet to find you today’s most fun/important/scary/fascinating stories about technology.
paragraphs.translation: 我已經搜遍網路，為你找出今天最有趣／最重要／最嚇人／最引人入勝的科技新聞。

paragraphs.text: 1 OpenAI has unveiled its long-awaited "super app" ChatGPT Work blends its chatbot, coding tool, and new models. (Reuters $) + It’s designed to do your work for you and with you. (Ars Technica) + And arrived the same day as OpenAI’s GPT 5.6 models. (NYT $) + It’s also developing a fully automated researcher. (MIT Technology Review) 2 Humanoids have performed teleoperated surgery on living animals In the world-first, they removed gallbladders from pigs. (Ars Technica) + The human work behind humanoids is hidden. (MIT Technology Review) 3 SK Hynix has landed the largest US listing by a foreign company The South Korean chip giant raised $26.5 billion. (CNN) + Demand for AI data centres has led its profits to skyrocket. (Guardian) + But its jumbo share sale may be a sign of overheated times. (FT $) + South Korea’s hottest bachelors are chip workers. (MIT Technology Review) 4 Tencent is leading a deal to unwind Meta's $2 billion Manus acquisition It’s in talks to become the Chinese AI startup’s largest shareholder. (FT $) + Tencent will reportedly buy Manus for no less ​than $2 billion. (Reuters $) + Beijing had ordered Meta to unwind the acquisition. (Bloomberg $) 5 Resuscitated human retinas responded to light 10 hours after death It’s a big step towards eye transplants that restore vision. (New Scientist $) + As is a new device that revives dead eyeballs. (MIT Technology Review) 6 Meta has started charging for AI access A new version of Muse Spark has a paid tier for developers. (Quartz) + Meta also plans to start producing an AI chip in September. (Reuters $) 7 OpenAI and Google have sold AI models to blacklisted China groups Via Singapore-based subsidiaries of Alibaba, Baidu and Tencent. (FT $) 8 A daughter tested an AI “death bot” of her father The technology provided both comfort and unease. (New Yorker $) 9 An astronomer says the hunt for alien life needs more statistics He wants to replace speculation with mathematical frameworks. (Quanta) 10 Pokémon Go players turned Times Square into a giant battlefield More than 1,500 fans finally fulfilled the game’s 2016 launch promise. (Wired $) + Pokémon Go is also training world models. (MIT Technology Review)
paragraphs.translation: 1 OpenAI 發表了眾所期待的「超級應用程式」ChatGPT Work 融合了聊天機器人、程式撰寫工具與新模型。（Reuters $）+ 它的設計是要替你完成工作，也和你一起工作。（Ars Technica）+ 而且與 OpenAI 的 GPT 5.6 模型同日推出。（NYT $）+ OpenAI 同時也在開發一款全自動化的研究員。（MIT Technology Review）2 人形機器人已對活體動物執行遠端遙控手術這是世界首例，牠們替豬隻摘除了膽囊。（Ars Technica）+ 人形機器人背後隱藏的人力工作。（MIT Technology Review） 3 SK 海力士完成外國企業在美國史上最大規模的上市這家南韓晶片巨頭募得 265 億美元。（CNN）+ AI 資料中心的需求讓其獲利暴增。（Guardian）+ 但這筆鉅額股票發行或許正是市場過熱的徵兆。（FT $）+ 南韓最搶手的單身漢是晶片工程師。（MIT Technology Review） 4 騰訊主導一筆交易，要撤銷 Meta 20 億美元收購 Manus 的案子騰訊正洽談成為這家中國 AI 新創公司最大股東。（FT $）+ 據報導騰訊將以不低於 20 億美元的價格收購 Manus。（Reuters $）+ 北京當局先前已下令 Meta 撤銷該收購案。（Bloomberg $） 5 復甦的人類視網膜在死亡 10 小時後仍對光線有反應這是邁向恢復視力的眼球移植的重要一步。（New Scientist $）+ 一款能讓死亡眼球復甦的新裝置也是如此。（MIT Technology Review） 6 Meta 開始針對 AI 使用收費新版 Muse Spark 針對開發者推出付費方案。（Quartz） + Meta 也計畫於 9 月開始生產 AI 晶片。（Reuters $） 7 OpenAI 與 Google 已將 AI 模型販售給被列入黑名單的中國企業透過阿里巴巴、百度與騰訊在新加坡設立的子公司進行。（FT $）8 一名女兒測試了以她父親打造的 AI「死亡機器人」這項技術同時帶來慰藉與不安。（New Yorker $）9 一位天文學家表示，尋找外星生命需要更多統計方法他希望以數學架構取代臆測。（Quanta）10 Pokémon Go 玩家把時代廣場變成一片巨大戰場超過 1,500 名玩家終於實現了這款遊戲 2016 年上市時的承諾。（Wired $）+ Pokémon Go 同時也在訓練世界模型。（MIT Technology Review）

paragraphs.text: Quote of the day
paragraphs.translation: 每日一句

paragraphs.text: “When we’re talking about AI, we love the hype, we get excited about it. The damn thing never actually lands in practice.”
paragraphs.translation: 「談到 AI 的時候，我們都很愛炒作話題、也為此感到興奮。但這東西實際上根本落不了地。」

paragraphs.text: —Vijay Janapa Reddi, an engineering professor at Harvard University, tells Wired why he’s skeptical about grand plans for AI.
paragraphs.translation: —哈佛大學工程學教授 Vijay Janapa Reddi 向《Wired》說明他為何對 AI 的宏大計畫抱持懷疑。

paragraphs.text: One More Thing
paragraphs.translation: 還有一件事

paragraphs.text: Why we should thank pigeons for our AI breakthroughs
paragraphs.translation: 我們為什麼該感謝鴿子促成了 AI 的突破

paragraphs.text: In 1943, psychologist B.F. Skinner led a secret government project to make bombs more precise. His idea: teach pigeons to guide missiles by pecking at targets on a screen inside a warhead. To train them, Skinner rewarded the birds with food when they made the right decisions, using trial and error to shape their behavior.
paragraphs.translation: 1943 年，心理學家 B.F. Skinner 主導了一項政府秘密計畫，目的是讓炸彈更精準命中目標。他的構想是：訓練鴿子在彈頭內的螢幕上啄擊目標，藉此引導飛彈。為了訓練這些鴿子，Skinner 在牠們做出正確判斷時給予食物獎勵，透過反覆試錯來塑造牠們的行為。

paragraphs.text: Unsurprisingly, the military never deployed Skinner’s kamikaze pigeons. Yet his experiments convinced him that pigeons were “an extremely reliable instrument” for studying learning.
paragraphs.translation: 不出所料，軍方從未真正部署 Skinner 的「神風鴿」。但這些實驗讓他深信，鴿子是研究學習機制「極為可靠的工具」。

paragraphs.text: Decades later, those same principles would help power reinforcement learning, the technology behind some of today’s most advanced AI systems.
paragraphs.translation: 數十年後，同樣的原理成為強化學習（reinforcement learning）的重要基礎，而強化學習正是當今部分最先進 AI 系統背後的核心技術。

paragraphs.text: Discover how pigeons inspired one of AI’s most powerful techniques.
paragraphs.translation: 深入了解鴿子如何啟發了 AI 最強大的技術之一。
